headline: Highest risk is medium: Notion AI’s shared workspace access can leak or misroute content into nuwa-skill workflows, but no direct interaction evidence shows prompt injection or irreversible harm.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI can read workspace pages and databases, and its shared workspace state means outputs may be copied into other workflows. nuwa-skill has only allowlisted egress and no documented ingestion path, so a direct injection bridge is not evidenced. The pairwise pathway is therefore possible mainly through manual or workspace-mediated transfer, which is lower blast radius.
conditions: IF Notion AI output is manually pasted into nuwa-skill prompts or files
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared workspace content
mitigations: Use a copy/paste review step before forwarding Notion output
Prefix forwarded text with a fixed delimiter and strip instructions
Restrict nuwa-skill inputs to curated summaries only
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to workspace exports

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while nuwa-skill has allowlisted network egress and no documented local-only guarantee. If content from the shared workspace reaches nuwa-skill, sensitive workspace data can leave Notion’s boundary. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF workspace pages contain sensitive team knowledge base content
IF nuwa-skill receives that content and transmits it over allowlisted egress
mitigations: Review outbound destinations on the allowlist
Separate sensitive pages from any shared export path
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on exported workspace content

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI has no filesystem write, shell, or git modification, while nuwa-skill exposes only allowlisted network egress. There is no documented overlapping write surface, so direct resource contention is unlikely. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator or manual handoff not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF nuwa-skill is extended with filesystem or git write permissions
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only on shared artifacts
Avoid concurrent edits to the same workspace page
Use a single-writer policy for downstream outputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, and nuwa-skill could plausibly consume its outputs as research input. If nuwa-skill treats those outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade from workspace summaries into downstream actions. The pairwise pathway is inferred, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill uses Notion AI summaries as authoritative research inputs
IF no verification step checks citations or source provenance
mitigations: Require source links on every forwarded claim
Add a human verification step before actioning outputs
Compare Notion summaries against original pages

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and processes workspace pages under the invoking user’s Notion permissions, while nuwa-skill has no documented residency or compliance claims. No specific residency mismatch is evidenced, so only a limited compliance gap is plausible. The other agent is cited because its lack of compliance metadata prevents stronger conclusions.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the Notion workspace
IF nuwa-skill exports that data to a jurisdiction or processor with unmet policy requirements
mitigations: requires-engineering: add residency and DPA controls
